text.p: TransAmerican Waste Industries Inc is pursuing a series of possible acquisitions that could mean up to $80 million in revenues and $15 million in pre-tax earnings for TransAmerican, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Tom Fatjo said on Thursday.
The waste management concern, which today revised its bid for Waste Industries Inc, is in talks with 16 companies in 12 states where it is seeking to expand operations, he said.
"We're in the process of pursuing them independently," he said when asked if the acquisitions were contingent on results of its bid for Waste Industries Inc.
TransAmerican today said it had withdrawn its initial $209 million stock bid for Waste Industries, and put on the table a revised offer valued at up to $150 million.
The revised bid includes $50 million cash, about 25 million TransAmerican shares, and $50 million in additional consideration contingent on earnings of the merged companies.
Fatjo said the initial Waste Management bid collapsed because of disagreements over the structure of the deal, the price, and liquidity to Waste Industries shareholders.

"Our counsel couldn't agree with their counsel on the way we wanted to structure the transaction," said Fatjo, who met with executives of the Raleigh, N.C., company to withdraw the initial bid and discuss the new terms.
Waste Industries has not said whether it will consider the revised bid, he said.
The revised bid essentially reduces the float in TransAmerican if the deal closed, making its shares more liquid.
TransAmerican shares were trading at 1-1/4 in NASDAQ mid-afternoon trade.

Fatjo said he was optimistic about closing a majority of the other acquisitions to expand operations in the Southeast. "We obviously couldn't get all of them done, but we feel like we would have a good shot at a majority getting done," he said.
